page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a bare metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family, featuring an AMD EPYC 9254 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz, supported by hyper-threading. Memory resources consist of 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a 960 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Benchmark results indicate strong computational and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core performance is in the top 25%. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves top 10% performance in PassMark memory testing, with read-only and write memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently placing in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top 10% performance in LLM inference text generation for both small and medium models, as well as top 10% speeds for small model prompt processing. However, static web serving throughput is moderate, placing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density and dedicated hardware access without virtualization overhead, making it efficient for workloads requiring sustained CPU and memory throughput. The combination of 48 dedicated vCPUs, fast DDR5 memory, and local SSD storage makes this server suitable for database operations, memory-intensive applications, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
